title: Ransomware data-recovery executive indicted for wire fraud after FBI sting
date_note: Krebs (20 Nov) says the indictment was returned "this week" in Rhode Island; 404 Media (19 Nov) says Wednesday, i.e. 18 Nov. The exact filing date is not stated.
summary: Krebs on Security reports that Juan Ricardo Palacio Escobar, co-founder of ransomwarehelp.com, was indicted for wire fraud in an indictment returned this week in Rhode Island. The indictment says the firm routinely paid ransomware groups for decryption keys. 404 Media reports prosecutors say the FBI posed as both a ransomware victim and the attacker in a sting.
plain: A ransomware data-recovery company allegedly paid the criminals for keys instead of using advanced tools. The FBI posed as a victim and as the attacker to catch it.
exec: Recovery firms that quietly pay ransoms may be doing so without telling clients; vet them before hiring in a crisis.
action: Before hiring a ransomware recovery firm, ask in writing whether it will pay the attackers and how it prices that, and report fraud to the FBI.

validation.note: Verify desk read Krebs (20 Nov) and the free lede of 404 Media (19 Nov, paywalled after). Both confirm the name, wire fraud and the FBI sting; Krebs adds routine payments to ransomware groups and Rhode Island. The "three counts", "Kansas business, $720,000" and "$445,000" claims could not be found in readable text and were removed. Each publisher states different facts, so kept single_source.

review.note: Could not verify from readable sources: 404 Media is paywalled after the lede (confirms name, Florida firm, FBI posed as victim and attacker) and Krebs (20 Nov) says only 'returned this week in Rhode Island', 'wire fraud', no count number, no Kansas business, no 720,000 USD charge and no 445,000 USD
